stem: A nurse manager reviewing retention data asks which nonretirement factor current NCSBN workforce findings identify most often as a reason nurses consider leaving. Which answer is best?

options.D: Lack of interest in professional development

rationale: NCSBN's 2026 workforce survey launch reports that stress and burnout were the most frequently selected nonretirement reason associated with nurses leaving or considering leaving, with workload and understaffing also prominent concerns.
educational_objective: Recognize major current nursing-workforce retention pressures identified by NCSBN.
source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
source_locator: Workforce survey announcement — stress/burnout most selected nonretirement reason; workload/understaffing among leading concerns
source_claim_supported: Current NCSBN workforce data identify stress/burnout as a leading nonretirement reason for leaving nursing.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Management of Care, printed p.7/PDF p.11
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — workforce retention and care environment
correction_summary: Replaced generic workforce assumptions with a current, directly stated NCSBN 2026 workforce finding.
